:::

This module runs automated data-quality checks (outliers, miscoded missing values, empty and constant columns, SPSS filter variables, category casing, problematic column names, mixed text encodings, spreadsheet formatting) on the extracted data files.
We examined 40 columns across 8 data files.
No file could be screened for careless responding.

**What this does not cover.** Only 0 of 8 data files could be screened: the rest had no detectable multi-item scale block, or too few respondents. Even in a screened file, these checks only look at multi-item rating scales — the only place where a repeated or flat answer pattern is interpretable. Single questions, open text, demographics and any item outside a detected scale block are never examined. A respondent can therefore answer most of a survey carelessly and still not be flagged here, and finding nothing is not evidence that a dataset is free of careless responding.

-  We classified 9 files: 9 data.
-  We found 9 tabular data files and extracted 40 columns from 8 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1).
-  The study-group step did not get an answer for 9 files (the model request failed); they were grouped by the fallback rules instead.
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (twoframes.rda: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: twoframes.rda. We ran automated data-quality checks on 40 columns and found no issues. We detected demographic column for Gender.
100% of columns are free text, not variables
